reference.source: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine / standard rheumatology references
clinicalPearls: A spectrum of dominantly inherited autoinflammatory diseases caused by gain-of-function variants in the NLRP3 gene encoding cryopyrin
Ranges in severity from mild familial cold autoinflammatory syndrome, through Muckle-Wells syndrome, to the most severe neonatal-onset multisystem inflammatory disease (NOMID/CINCA)
An urticaria-like rash that is typically non-pruritic, together with fever and conjunctivitis, is a hallmark across the spectrum
Cold exposure often triggers flares in the milder end of the spectrum
Progressive sensorineural hearing loss is characteristic of Muckle-Wells syndrome and the more severe forms
Severe disease features chronic aseptic meningitis, raised intracranial pressure, developmental delay, and a characteristic bony overgrowth arthropathy of the knees
IL-1 blockade produces dramatic clinical and biochemical improvement, reflecting the central role of interleukin-1 beta
Secondary AA amyloidosis is a recognised long-term complication of inadequately controlled disease
reference.pathophysiology: Activating mutations in NLRP3 render the NLRP3 (cryopyrin) inflammasome hyperactive, leading to constitutive caspase-1 activation and unregulated secretion of interleukin-1 beta. The resulting systemic and organ-specific inflammation affects skin, joints, eyes, the inner ear, and the central nervous system, with severity correlating broadly with the degree of inflammasome dysregulation.
additionalDifferentials: Other periodic fever syndromes (FMF, TRAPS, HIDS)
Systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis / adult-onset Still disease
Chronic infectious or autoimmune meningitis in the severe forms
additionalInvestigations: NLRP3 genetic testing (including screening for somatic mosaicism when suspicion is high but germline testing negative)
Acute-phase reactants (CRP, ESR, serum amyloid A)
Audiometry to detect and monitor sensorineural hearing loss
Ophthalmological assessment for conjunctivitis, uveitis, and papilloedema
Lumbar puncture and neuroimaging in severe forms with CNS involvement
redFlags: Progressive hearing loss indicating ongoing uncontrolled inflammation
Raised intracranial pressure or chronic meningitis in severe neonatal-onset disease
reference.prognosis: IL-1 targeted therapy has transformed outcomes, halting or improving hearing loss and CNS inflammation when started early; untreated severe disease can cause permanent deafness, neurological disability, and amyloidosis, whereas the mildest cold-induced form has a relatively benign course.
pitfalls: Misdiagnosing the rash as ordinary allergic urticaria and prescribing antihistamines alone
Missing somatic mosaicism when standard germline NLRP3 testing is negative
Delaying IL-1 therapy in severe forms and allowing irreversible hearing or neurological damage
Failing to monitor for amyloidosis in long-standing disease
management: Treat with interleukin-1 targeted therapy such as anakinra, canakinumab or rilonacept as the disease-specific mainstay that controls inflammation across the spectrum
Start IL-1 inhibition early in severe forms to halt or prevent sensorineural hearing loss and central nervous system damage
In milder familial cold autoinflammatory disease, advise avoidance of cold exposure that triggers flares
Monitor disease activity with acute-phase reactants (CRP and serum amyloid A) and serial audiometry for hearing loss
Undertake ophthalmological assessment for conjunctivitis, uveitis and papilloedema, and manage raised intracranial pressure in NOMID/CINCA
Screen for AA amyloidosis with urinalysis for proteinuria and renal function monitoring
Provide genetic counselling for this autosomal dominant NLRP3 disorder with family testing
